description:
Imagine a busy manager who runs a team-building bowling game with a bed sheet hung across the lane. Your team bowls blind, and the scores arrive six months later. That is the default office, and it is the problem The New One Minute Manager by Kenneth H. Blanchard and Spencer Johnson sets out to fix.
This is a summary and analysis of the book's three one-minute tools: the one-page goal, the one-minute praise, and the one-minute redirect. We also cover the failure states the parable warns about, the leave-alone zap and gunny sacking, and the one counterpoint worth taking seriously: the neat three-step formula can feel strained in a remote, fragmented workplace.
